sourceObservations.notes: Inclusive causal attention uses j <= i, including the current token. The initial x-weighted sum is a simplified identity-value representation. Softmax normalizes eligible keys for each fixed query.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Row projections q=xWQ, k=xWK, v=xWV have distinct matching and content roles. Queries and keys must share width for their dot product.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Step 2 already divides the dot product by sqrt(dk); Step 3 repeats the description and must not add a second division. Learned WO is a linear projection, not a value-preserving reshape. Weighted values follow score softmax.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: The third output compares q3 with k1,k2,k3, includes its own value, combines normalized values, then projects. Some diagram labels use dv at query/key nodes; general dot-product compatibility requires dk, not forced equality with dv.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Parallel heads at the same depth use separate learned Q/K/V projections. The architecture permits distinct patterns but does not guarantee learned specialization.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Every head applies scaled attention, then outputs are concatenated and multiplied by WO. The context shorthand omits the current token in its bracket but the explicit sum includes j <= i.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Four illustrated heads concatenate to width A*dv, then WO has shape A*dv by d. With dv=d/A this is d by d. Head 4 visibly has WK3 rather than WK4: a reused label, not a shared-key constraint.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Additive pre-norm residual streams accumulate the input and sublayer outputs. Each token has a stream; attention couples eligible token information between streams.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Explicit pre-norm order and residual branch states t1 through t5. FFN is ReLU(t4 W1+b1)W2+b2, a position-wise two-projection network.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Per-token feature normalization has learned gain and offset; printed formula omits epsilon. Two pre-normalization stages and residual additions are shown. All-N attention argument requires the previously specified causal mask in decoder use.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Pack N row embeddings into N by d. Q,K are N by dk and V is N by dv. Row computations can be vectorized for known inputs, not independently generate unknown future token IDs.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Dense N by N score table masked strictly above the diagonal with negative infinity; zero additive entries elsewhere. Softmax makes forbidden weights zero. The current token remains eligible.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Diagram shows projected Q/K/V and NxN scores. Its note explicitly omits scaling and softmax from the sketch; do not execute the displayed masked infinities times V literally.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Vectorized head index denotes a whole N by dv output matrix, not one token. Concat and WO precede the additive residual and second normalized FFN branch. H=X when both branch outputs vanish.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Word-level example Janet will back the bill has five IDs and five one-hot rows. ID5 with four preceding zeros is consistent with one-based indexing; not a universal tokenizer convention.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: One-hot W times vocabulary-by-d embedding E selects token rows. A learned absolute-position table is added elementwise in this design. Neither five positions nor learned absolute embeddings are universal requirements.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Tied unembedding uses E transpose; final context row gives raw vocabulary logits, then softmax. Tying is a design choice, not universal. Vocabulary softmax differs from attention-key softmax.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Final-layer last-position row h_N supplies the next-token head. Greedy decoding takes the argmax, not stochastic categorical sampling. PDF link points to the public Transformer Explainer, which documents a live GPT-2 model; its page was read but model inference was not executed.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

sourceObservations.notes: Top-k retains highest k then renormalizes. Top-p sorts descending and takes the shortest prefix reaching cumulative p. Printed percent prose and 0-to-1 inequality use different scales; p=.9 means 90 percent. The threshold is inclusive in the printed inequality.
sourceObservations.method: Personally viewed actual page pixels, with extracted text cross-check; not extraction-only.

answers.reasoning: The timeline distinguishes visual representations, vision plus language, and vision/language connected to actions.
The memory-network entry is external readable/writable memory, not a historical priority claim.
Next-token conditioning uses the known prefix and appends the chosen token.
The source examples are GPT decoder-only, BERT/ViT encoder-style, and translation encoder-decoder.
The diagram orders embedding plus position, transformer stack, then language-model head.
An identical static lookup vector cannot by itself encode a context-specific pronoun referent.
Only the available prefix can contribute, not unseen continuation words.
The explicit sum and diagram include j=i and exclude j>i.
For each fixed query, softmax runs across its eligible key scores.
Query specifies matching demand, key provides compatibility, value supplies weighted content.
Row multiplication requires d by dk for query/key and d by dv for value.
The dot product is 6 and sqrt(4)=2, so the scaled score is 3.
The source equation already scales the score; the second verbal step is not a second division.
Each independent product has mean zero and variance one; the sum has variance dk and division by sqrt(dk) divides variance by dk.
Exponentials are 1 and 3, weights 1/4 and 3/4, so the output is (0.5,3).
WO is a learned linear mixing map into the residual-stream width, not merely a reshape.
q3 matches k1 through k3; normalized weights combine v1 through v3 and WO projects.
Both dot-product operands have dk=8 entries; dv=5 concerns the value output.
Independent learned projections permit separate subspaces and attention patterns without guaranteeing they differ.
Head vectors concatenate first, then WO mixes/projects them.
4*16=64 concatenated entries, so WO is 64 by 64.
Two heads have 2*3*8*4=192 projection weights, plus (2*4)*8=64 output weights, total 256.
Attention branch outputs carry eligible cross-token information into otherwise separate streams.
The shown pre-norm sequence is LN, attention, addition, LN, FFN, addition.
The nonlinearity occurs between the two affine maps.
Hidden preactivation is (1,-1), ReLU gives (1,0), second map gives (2,1), and bias gives (3,0).
Mean and population variance are over a token vector feature coordinates, not batch examples or future tokens.
Mean is 2, variance is 1, yielding (-1,1) under the stated epsilon-free calculation.
Coordinatewise gain and offset give (-2+1,3-1)=(-1,2).
Positive epsilon prevents division by zero and stabilizes near-zero variance, though nonzero small variance is not mathematically undefined.
Earlier equations normalize before each sublayer; the original diagram shows Add & Norm afterward.
Each row is one input token represented by d feature values.
Six token rows remain; Q,K widths are 3 and V width is 5.
Known-sequence attention outputs at one layer can be computed in parallel with a causal mask; future token IDs are not independent.
Mask entries are negative infinity for j>i and zero otherwise.
Inclusive lower triangle has 1+2+3+4+5=15 eligible pairs.
A zero score has exponential one, so it is not excluded; negative infinity has exponential zero.
Second scores are (0,1/sqrt(2)); weights are approximately (0.33023845,0.66976155), giving (0.6604769,2.6790462).
The first row has exactly one eligible finite score, whose normalized weight is one, so it returns v1.
Scale and mask scores, then normalize each query row before the matrix product with values.
Dense entries scale as N squared: 10000 to 40000, fourfold.
A vectorized head output includes all N positions and has shape N by dv.
Both additive branch outputs vanish, leaving the original X.
There is one vocabulary-wide row per token: 5 by 300.
Four preceding zeros put the one in the fifth entry, matching one-based ID 5.
Five word-level tokens describe this example only; other tokenizers can split words or punctuation.
The one-hot rows select E row 2 then row 1, giving ((3,4),(1,2)).
Elementwise addition yields ((3.1,4.2),(1.3,2.4)).
Position vectors introduce ordering information alongside token identity.
Learned absolute positions describe this design; other positional encodings also exist.
A row of width 64 needs a 64 by 1000 projection for 1000 logits.
Transposition shares the embedding parameters with the output projection.
Softmax turns unrestricted real scores into positive normalized probabilities.
The logits are (0,ln2,ln3); exponentials (1,2,3) normalize by six.
The next-token head uses the final layer representation at the current last prefix position N.
Greedy selection chooses A deterministically for fixed scores with no tie.
Top-k retains the k highest-probability candidates.
The retained mass is .8; divide .5 and .3 by .8 to obtain .625 and .375.
Sort descending, then choose the shortest prefix with cumulative mass at least p.
Exact .5+.3=.8 meets the inclusive threshold; retain two and normalize by .8.
The first distribution reaches .8 at one token; the second reaches only .75 at two, requiring three.
Ninety percent is the unit-interval threshold .9.
Renormalization divides by retained mass, preserving relative weights before sampling.
Encoder input attention has no left-to-right causal restriction, though other masks may apply.
Cross-attention queries come from the decoder and key/value memory from the encoder.
The decoder adds an attention sublayer over the encoder outputs.
Available image patches can share global context without autoregressive left-to-right masking.
